scenes: Yes. Steel rails expand in the heat and can buckle, | so trains slow down. | Roads soften, and hot, thin air means planes need longer runways.
That means slower journeys, missed shifts and late supplies, | including medicines and food on their way to the people who need them.
Infrastructure built for the heat to come.
